change","user":{"login":"IanFrelinger","id":16062048,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE2MDYyMDQ4","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/16062048?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger","html_url":"https://github.com/IanFrelinger","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/IanFrelinger/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":" ## Summary `Ashlar.Authoring` no longer depends on `Ashlar.Hosting`. A brick project's first restore on an empty cache goes from **144 packages and 998 MiB** to **30 packages and 144 MiB**. The public API of `Ashlar.Authoring` is unchanged: `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` is untouched and `BrickAuthoringPublicApiSnapshotTests` passes. Owner-delegated decision row 9 in #861 covers this change. ## Measurement The numbers come from `scripts/measure-authoring-restore-footprint.sh`, which is new in this PR. It packs the graph (in `local` mode), creates a net8.0 project that references only `Ashlar.Authoring`, restores it into an empty `NUGET_PACKAGES`, and counts what landed. I ran it in the devtest container, on SDK 10.0.401. | | Packages | Size | |---|---|---| | 0.3.0 from nuget.org (`published 0.3.0`) | 144 | 1,047,514,056 bytes (998 MiB) | | master packed locally (`local`) | 144 | 998 MiB | | this branch packed locally (`local 9.9.9-after`) | 30 | 151,243,112 bytes (144 MiB) | | an empty net8.0 project, for reference | 2 | 67 MiB | Of the 144 MiB, 67 MiB are the two .NET reference packs (`microsoft.netcore.app.ref` and `microsoft.aspnetcore.app.ref`), which an empty net8.0 project also restores on this SDK. Ashlar's own share therefore drops from about 931 MiB to about 77 MiB. Most of what remains comes from `Ashlar.Core.Application`: System.Reactive, FluentValidation, MediatR, and NSec with libsodium (through `Certification.Contracts`). Those packages appear in the public types of `Ashlar.Core.Application` and are used in 18 files, so removing them would be a breaking change, and I stopped there. ## How - `AddAshlarBrick()` used to call `AddAshlarSdk(sdk => sdk.RegisterBrick())` from `Ashlar.Hosting`. It now registers a `BrickTypeRegistration(typeof(T))` singleton. - `BrickTypeRegistration` is a new public sealed class in `Ashlar.Core.Domain.Bricks`, which `Ashlar.Authoring` already references. - Both brick-registry builders in `AdaptationServiceCollectionExtensions` read the same list: first the types from `AdaptationBrickOptions.AdditionalBrickTypes`, which `AddAshlarSdk` and `AddAdaptationBricks` feed, then every `BrickTypeRegistration`. - The `BrickRegistry` factory and the certified-catalog bootstrap share one helper, `AdditionalBrickTypes(sp)`. - `Ashlar.Authoring.csproj` drops the `ProjectReference` to `Ashlar.Hosting`. Its package description now says that a host referencing it also needs `Ashlar.Hosting.Bundle`. - Side effect: `AddAshlarBrick` no longer registers an empty `AshlarSdkOptions` singleton. ## Integrator decisions (open in the next handoff) - **Brick order changes.** Bricks added with `AddAshlarBrick` now come after the `AddAshlarSdk`/`AddAdaptationBricks` types in `GetAllBricks()`. Before, they were interleaved in registration order. - **Migration.** A host that calls `AddAshlar()` and referenced only `Ashlar.Authoring` must now add `Ashlar.Hosting.Bundle`. - This is a dependency change, not an API change, and the CHANGELOG describes it. - The consumer template's host already references the Bundle, and so do `verify-external-product-shape.sh` and the scaffold. ## Docs and records - `CHANGELOG.md` gets the "Changed" entry with the measured numbers and the migration. - `consumer-template/CONSUMING.md`: - step 4 says the host also references `Ashlar.Hosting.Bundle`; - the "about 1 GB" note is scoped to 0.3.0, with the 0.4.0 number added; - the paragraph on how `Ashlar.Infrastructure` reaches a host is corrected. - `docs/AuthoringBricks.md`: the "Registering in a host" section and the `AddAshlarBrick` paragraph no longer say it is "exactly `AddAshlarSdk`". - `samples/certified-brick-reuse/README.md`: the dependency note now says Hosting was a dependency up to 0.3.0. - `CertifierReferenceSet` comments and `CertifierReferenceSetTests` docs: they said Authoring pulls in Hosting and Infrastructure, which is no longer true. Behaviour is unchanged: Authoring is still not anchored, and the reason is restated. - The knowledge graph is regenerated. ## Testing All of this ran in the devtest container. - `dotnet build Ashlar.sln`: 0 errors. - `Tests.Infrastructure` (adaptation registration, hosting smoke, certifier reference set, capability routing): 52/52 passed. - `Tests.Application`: 442/442 passed. - `Mcp.Server.Tests`: 55/55 passed. - `Tests.CLI`: 352/352 passed. - New tests: - `BrickTypeRegistration_reaches_the_registry_after_the_option_types`; - `AddAshlarBrick_then_AddAshlar_puts_the_brick_in_the_registry`, which goes end to end through the real `AddAshlar()`; - `BrickTypeRegistrationTests` in `Ashlar.Tests.Domain`, which keeps `Ashlar.Core.Domain` at the kernel gate's 100% line coverage. - Mutation `registry-ignores-brick-type-registrations` (removes the `BrickTypeRegistration` read): **KILLED**. The red run failed 2 of 14 tests (both new tests); the green run passed 14 of 14 at commit 33b5c6f52. - `bash scripts/ci/run-repo-gates.sh`: all 40 gates passed. - `verify-knowledge-graph-current.py`: current. ## Also fixed: a flaky MCP audit test - `BrickMcpToolContributorTests.Invoke_executes_deterministically_...` failed once on the Windows readiness lane ([run 40213630003](https://github.com/IanFrelinger/Ashlar/actions/runs/40213630003)). - It asserted that the audit record does not contain `ada` anywhere. But the record carries a sha256 of a result that includes a random audit id, and that hex read `...777adaf...`. - The assertion now checks for the quoted argument value `"ada"` and the output value `hi ada`. - This PR's change did not cause the failure. The fixed test passes 10/10 in the container.
